walkthroughs.body_html: Open clusters like the Pleiades are young (tens to hundreds of millions of years). Their HR diagrams show a complete main sequence and bright blue stars still present.
Globular clusters are ancient (10-13 Gyr) and metal-poor. Their HR diagrams show only the lower main sequence — massive stars have already evolved off — plus a clear giant branch.
Comparing the turnoff luminosity with theoretical isochrones gives the cluster age. Hotter turnoffs mean younger clusters; the oldest globulars approach the age of the universe itself.
